Title_or_Action: Certain administrative transactions prohibited by Directive 4 under EO 14024
Primary_Beneficiaries: U.S. persons operating lawfully in Russia; Russian government entities receiving routine taxes and fees
What_It_Authorized: Payment of taxes, fees, import duties, permits, licenses, registrations, certifications and similar day-to-day administrative transactions
Predecessor_or_Context: Successor in a long-running GL 13 series
Correct_Evidentiary_Classification: Technical administrative carveout; limited transactional relief
Russian_Reception_or_Benefit: Allowed routine payments to Russian state bodies and avoided forced shutdown of lawful U.S. operations
What_It_Does_Not_Prove: Does not remove sanctions on the Central Bank, Ministry of Finance or National Wealth Fund; does not authorize broad investment or financing
Records_Needed: OFAC decision memo; transaction-volume data; requests from U.S. companies; comparison with prior GL 13 versions

Title_or_Action: Petroleum services and other transactions related to the Caspian Pipeline Consortium and Tengizchevroil
Primary_Beneficiaries: Kazakhstan; CPC shareholders; Tengizchevroil; Western energy firms; Russian transit and service counterparties
What_It_Authorized: Specified petroleum services and otherwise prohibited transactions necessary for CPC and Tengiz operations
Predecessor_or_Context: Implemented exceptions to the February 2025 petroleum-services prohibition; later amended as 124A and 124B
Correct_Evidentiary_Classification: Narrow multinational energy-security carveout, not general Russia oil relief
Russian_Reception_or_Benefit: Preserved throughput and fees involving Russian territory and infrastructure while protecting Kazakh exports and Western investments
What_It_Does_Not_Prove: Does not authorize general Russian petroleum services or remove sanctions on unrelated Russian producers
Records_Needed: Project payment flows; Russian transit revenues; lobbying and national-security rationale; beneficial effect by shareholder

Title_or_Action: Certain services related to Sakhalin-2
Primary_Beneficiaries: Japanese utilities and energy security; Sakhalin-2 participants; Russian project entities
What_It_Authorized: Specified services related to Sakhalin-2 that would otherwise be prohibited
Predecessor_or_Context: Continuation of prior Sakhalin-2 licenses; later extended through 55E and 55F
Correct_Evidentiary_Classification: Project-specific continuity license with material Russian-project benefit and allied energy rationale
Russian_Reception_or_Benefit: Allowed the project to continue receiving specified services and preserved revenue and operations while reducing disruption to Japan
What_It_Does_Not_Prove: Does not constitute broad sanctions removal or authorize unrelated Russian oil and gas projects
Records_Needed: Japanese request records; project revenues; U.S. interagency decision papers; Russian fiscal benefit

Title_or_Action: Certain transactions related to civil nuclear energy
Primary_Beneficiaries: U.S. and allied nuclear operators; uranium, fuel-cycle and civil-nuclear supply chains; Russian nuclear counterparties
What_It_Authorized: Specified civil-nuclear transactions otherwise restricted under Russia sovereign-transactions rules
Predecessor_or_Context: Continuation of GL 115A; later amended through 115C and 115D; Paks II later received separate GL 132
Correct_Evidentiary_Classification: Civil-nuclear supply and safety carveout; real Russian commercial benefit with non-Russian energy and safety rationale
Russian_Reception_or_Benefit: Maintained permitted civil-nuclear transactions involving Russian entities and the Central Bank in specified circumstances
What_It_Does_Not_Prove: Does not authorize military nuclear cooperation or erase Rosatom-related restrictions outside the license
Records_Needed: Transaction counterparties; Paks II overlap; payments to Russian entities; interagency nonproliferation and energy-security rationale

Title_or_Action: Certain administrative transactions prohibited by Directive 4 under EO 14024
Primary_Beneficiaries: Same category as GL 13M
What_It_Authorized: Continued routine taxes, fees, permits, licenses and administrative payments
Predecessor_or_Context: Successor to GL 13M
Correct_Evidentiary_Classification: Technical continuation; should not be counted as an independent strategic concession equal to battlefield or diplomatic decisions
Russian_Reception_or_Benefit: Continued limited state-revenue and administrative flows
What_It_Does_Not_Prove: Does not authorize general dealings with blocked Russian sovereign institutions
Records_Needed: Change log from GL 13M; actual transaction totals; industry requests

Title_or_Action: Cyber-related designation of AEZA Group and associated infrastructure
Primary_Beneficiaries: U.S. and allied cybersecurity interests
What_It_Authorized: Blocked Russia-linked cybercrime hosting and associated persons/entities
Predecessor_or_Context: First notable new Russia-linked designation of the second term in the original J20 ledger
Correct_Evidentiary_Classification: Direct coercive action against Russia-linked cybercrime infrastructure
Russian_Reception_or_Benefit: Russian actors lost access to property and U.S. financial channels; action contradicted a no-pressure narrative
What_It_Does_Not_Prove: Does not establish comprehensive pressure on Russian state cyber operations or measure enforcement success
Records_Needed: Asset blocks; seizures; service disruption; enforcement follow-through

Title_or_Action: Transactions related to meetings between the U.S. and Russian governments in Alaska
Primary_Beneficiaries: U.S. and Russian officials, carriers, vendors, diplomatic and logistical providers
What_It_Authorized: Transactions ordinarily incident and necessary to the Alaska summit
Predecessor_or_Context: Issued two days before the August 15 summit
Correct_Evidentiary_Classification: Diplomatic-meeting facilitation; symbolic normalization but routine legal necessity for sanctioned counterparties
Russian_Reception_or_Benefit: Enabled Russian delegation travel, lodging, logistics and summit operations on U.S. soil
What_It_Does_Not_Prove: Does not itself grant economic sanctions relief beyond summit-related transactions or prove secret concessions
Records_Needed: Authorized vendors; covered Russian entities; costs; additional licenses or waivers linked to summit

Title_or_Action: Additional 25 percent tariff on Indian imports tied to Russian-oil purchases
Primary_Beneficiaries: U.S. coercive-policy interests; indirectly Ukraine and sanctions coalition
What_It_Authorized: Imposed additional tariff because India imported Russian oil
Predecessor_or_Context: Signed before Alaska summit; effective after summit
Correct_Evidentiary_Classification: Implemented secondary economic pressure, though delayed effectiveness created a negotiation window
Russian_Reception_or_Benefit: Raised cost to a major Russian-oil purchaser and signaled possible secondary measures
What_It_Does_Not_Prove: Does not prove reduced Russian revenue without shipping and trade data; burden fell directly on India
Records_Needed: India commitment text; customs collections; oil-flow data; summit-related delay rationale

Title_or_Action: Major Russian oil-company sanctions
Primary_Beneficiaries: Rosneft, Lukoil and 50-percent-owned entities
What_It_Authorized: Blocked property and interests in property and imposed sanctions risk
Predecessor_or_Context: First major direct Russia oil sanctions of the second term; paired with GLs 124A and 126-128
Correct_Evidentiary_Classification: Major direct coercive action against core Russian energy interests
Russian_Reception_or_Benefit: Raised financing, insurance, trading, ownership and divestment risks for two major producers
What_It_Does_Not_Prove: Does not prove effective revenue reduction without enforcement and evasion data
Records_Needed: Blocked assets; trade displacement; enforcement cases; predesignation warnings and lobbying

Title_or_Action: CPC and Tengiz transactions involving Rosneft or Lukoil interests
Primary_Beneficiaries: Kazakhstan, Western oil companies, CPC and Tengiz participants
What_It_Authorized: Preserved specified CPC/Tengiz transactions despite Rosneft/Lukoil designations
Predecessor_or_Context: Amended GL 124 on designation day
Correct_Evidentiary_Classification: Collateral-impact carveout preserving non-Russian production and transit; also protects some Russia-linked interests
Russian_Reception_or_Benefit: Reduced spillover from oil-company sanctions and preserved Russian transit-linked operations
What_It_Does_Not_Prove: Does not cancel Rosneft/Lukoil designations or permit unrelated transactions
Records_Needed: Ownership and revenue allocation; interagency energy-market analysis

Title_or_Action: Wind down transactions involving Rosneft or Lukoil
Primary_Beneficiaries: Customers, banks, employees, suppliers and counterparties exiting blocked relationships
What_It_Authorized: Time-limited wind-down transactions
Predecessor_or_Context: Issued with designations
Correct_Evidentiary_Classification: Standard sanctions wind-down protection
Russian_Reception_or_Benefit: Prevented disorderly market disruption and allowed contractual exit
What_It_Does_Not_Prove: Does not provide indefinite operating authority or erase blocking sanctions
Records_Needed: Wind-down payments; extensions; compliance reports

Title_or_Action: Debt, equity and derivative transactions involving Rosneft or Lukoil
Primary_Beneficiaries: Investors and financial institutions unwinding securities exposure
What_It_Authorized: Time-limited divestment and transfer of covered debt, equity and derivatives to non-U.S. persons under conditions
Predecessor_or_Context: Issued with designations
Correct_Evidentiary_Classification: Standard market-exit license
Russian_Reception_or_Benefit: Allowed orderly disposition and reduced harm to nonblocked investors
What_It_Does_Not_Prove: Does not authorize new investment in the companies or payment of value to blocked owners beyond license terms
Records_Needed: Securities transfers; buyers; proceeds controls

Title_or_Action: Transactions involving Lukoil retail service stations outside Russia
Primary_Beneficiaries: Consumers, employees, suppliers and host countries
What_It_Authorized: Specified operation and maintenance of non-Russian retail stations
Predecessor_or_Context: Issued with Lukoil designation; amended through 128A, 128B and 128C
Correct_Evidentiary_Classification: Consumer and foreign-economy carveout with continuing Lukoil-network value
Russian_Reception_or_Benefit: Preserved operations and employment at non-Russian stations while later versions addressed ownership and duration
What_It_Does_Not_Prove: Does not broadly authorize Lukoil upstream operations or unrestricted remittance to Russia
Records_Needed: Station ownership; cash controls; remittances; divestment efforts

Title_or_Action: CPC, Tengizchevroil and Karachaganak projects
Primary_Beneficiaries: Kazakhstan, Western investors and specified Russia-linked interests
What_It_Authorized: Expanded project coverage to Karachaganak and continued petroleum-service authorizations
Predecessor_or_Context: Amendment after Rosneft/Lukoil designations
Correct_Evidentiary_Classification: Multinational energy-security carveout with measurable Russian-linked benefit
Russian_Reception_or_Benefit: Preserved exports, transit and project operations involving Russian geography or ownership
What_It_Does_Not_Prove: Does not authorize general services to the Russian petroleum sector
Records_Needed: Project-level Russian revenues and ownership; allied-government requests

Title_or_Action: Lukoil retail stations outside Russia
Primary_Beneficiaries: Non-Russian retail operations
What_It_Authorized: Amended operation authority
Predecessor_or_Context: Successor to GL 128
Correct_Evidentiary_Classification: Operational continuity, not blanket sanctions relief
Russian_Reception_or_Benefit: Continued non-Russian station activity
What_It_Does_Not_Prove: Does not unfreeze Lukoil generally
Records_Needed: Revenue controls; changes from GL 128

Title_or_Action: Certain Lukoil entities in Bulgaria
Primary_Beneficiaries: Bulgarian refinery, fuel market, employees and government
What_It_Authorized: Specified transactions involving named Bulgarian entities
Predecessor_or_Context: Issued after designation amid Bulgarian energy-security concerns
Correct_Evidentiary_Classification: Host-country energy-security carveout with direct operational benefit to Lukoil-linked assets
Russian_Reception_or_Benefit: Prevented immediate disruption of Bulgaria’s fuel system and preserved asset value pending resolution
What_It_Does_Not_Prove: Does not authorize unrestricted transfer of proceeds to blocked Russian owners
Records_Needed: Bulgarian control arrangements; payment restrictions; divestment plans

Title_or_Action: Negotiation and contingent sale contracts for Lukoil International GmbH
Primary_Beneficiaries: Potential nonblocked purchasers; host countries; employees; creditors
What_It_Authorized: Negotiation and entry into contingent contracts plus maintenance pending sale
Predecessor_or_Context: Issued to facilitate divestment of international assets
Correct_Evidentiary_Classification: Divestment facilitation that can preserve value while separating assets from blocked ownership
Russian_Reception_or_Benefit: Allowed sale negotiations and maintenance rather than forced collapse
What_It_Does_Not_Prove: Does not authorize consummation without further conditions or unrestricted proceeds to Lukoil
Records_Needed: Bidders; valuations; political contacts; proceeds escrow and ownership transition

Title_or_Action: Transactions involving Paks II civil nuclear power plant
Primary_Beneficiaries: Hungary, Rosatom-linked project entities and civil-nuclear suppliers
What_It_Authorized: Authorized Paks II transactions otherwise prohibited by Russia sovereign-transactions restrictions
Predecessor_or_Context: Separate project-specific license after GL 115B
Correct_Evidentiary_Classification: Specific Russian-backed state project authorization with Hungarian energy-policy rationale
Russian_Reception_or_Benefit: Allowed a major Rosatom-linked project to proceed in an EU/NATO state
What_It_Does_Not_Prove: Does not authorize broader Rosatom military or unrelated commercial activity
Records_Needed: Hungarian and Russian requests; project payments; U.S. strategic rationale

Title_or_Action: Lukoil retail stations outside Russia
Primary_Beneficiaries: Non-Russian station network
What_It_Authorized: Extended or amended retail-station authority
Predecessor_or_Context: Successor to GL 128A
Correct_Evidentiary_Classification: Targeted operational relief; not cancellation of Lukoil sanctions
Russian_Reception_or_Benefit: Maintained asset operations into 2026
What_It_Does_Not_Prove: Does not remove Lukoil from SDN list
Records_Needed: Duration rationale; station revenues; divestment progress

Title_or_Action: Sakhalin-2 and civil-nuclear extensions
Primary_Beneficiaries: Japanese energy users; civil-nuclear operators; Russian counterparties
What_It_Authorized: Extended existing project-specific authorizations
Predecessor_or_Context: Successors to GL 55D and 115B
Correct_Evidentiary_Classification: Continuation of allied-energy and civil-nuclear carveouts
Russian_Reception_or_Benefit: Preserved specified Russian-project revenue and operations
What_It_Does_Not_Prove: Does not amount to general sanctions normalization
Records_Needed: Interagency reviews; transaction volumes; allied requests

Title_or_Action: Original J20 sanctions-relief score
Primary_Beneficiaries: Mixed stakeholders
What_It_Authorized: The ledger counted five spring/summer licenses and later Lukoil authorizations as Russia-benefiting actions
Predecessor_or_Context: Must be compared against inherited authorizations, allied interests, October designations and wind-down norms
Correct_Evidentiary_Classification: The pattern shows reluctance to impose major new direct sanctions before October and willingness to preserve selected Russian-linked activity; it does not support treating every license as an equal strategic concession
Russian_Reception_or_Benefit: Russia obtained project-specific and administrative continuity while major coercive designations arrived later
What_It_Does_Not_Prove: Does not establish that technical licenses were issued as favors or that sanctions policy was uniformly pro-Russian
Records_Needed: Full OFAC licensing docket; applicant identities; interagency recommendations; lobbying contacts; transaction amounts

Title_or_Action: Delivery and sale of Russian-origin crude oil and petroleum products to India
Primary_Beneficiaries: Indian refiners and consumers; shippers, insurers and banks; Russian sellers and fiscal interests
What_It_Authorized: Specified transactions necessary to deliver and sell qualifying Russian-origin cargoes loaded by the stated date
Predecessor_or_Context: Issued during Iran-war supply disruption; one day before public reporting of Russian targeting support
Correct_Evidentiary_Classification: Temporary energy-market authorization with real Russian transaction and revenue benefit
Russian_Reception_or_Benefit: Preserved delivery, settlement and sale pathways for qualifying Russian cargoes during a major energy shock
What_It_Does_Not_Prove: Does not delist Russian oil companies, authorize all Russian oil trade or prove reward motive
Records_Needed: Decision memo; date officials learned of Russian targeting support; cargo values; counterparties; alternative supply analysis

Title_or_Action: Delivery and sale of Russian-origin crude oil and petroleum products
Primary_Beneficiaries: Global energy purchasers and market participants; Russian sellers and fiscal interests
What_It_Authorized: Specified delivery and sale transactions for cargoes loaded by the stated date
Predecessor_or_Context: Issued after public targeting-assistance reporting and Trump's March 7 minimization; later superseded by 134A
Correct_Evidentiary_Classification: Temporary market-stabilization license; material Russian revenue pathway
Russian_Reception_or_Benefit: Continued qualifying Russian oil sales after the targeting allegation was public
What_It_Does_Not_Prove: Does not repeal the Russia sanctions regime or establish a quid pro quo
Records_Needed: Interagency decision record; oil-price forecast; targeting-intelligence knowledge; transaction and revenue data

Title_or_Action: Amended Russian-origin oil delivery and sale authorization
Primary_Beneficiaries: Same market participants and Russian counterparties as GL 134
What_It_Authorized: Extended or amended qualifying cargo and transaction authority
Predecessor_or_Context: Superseded GL 134; expired April 11, 2026
Correct_Evidentiary_Classification: Extension of temporary Russian-oil relief with supply-stability rationale
Russian_Reception_or_Benefit: Preserved qualifying cargo delivery and sale pathways after Russian denials and continuing intelligence concern
What_It_Does_Not_Prove: Does not authorize unrestricted future purchases or remove entity designations
Records_Needed: Change log; cargo values; beneficiaries; White House and Treasury approvals

Title_or_Action: Continued Russian-origin oil delivery and sale authorization
Primary_Beneficiaries: Energy-market participants; Russian sellers; importing states
What_It_Authorized: Continued specified delivery and sale transactions
Predecessor_or_Context: Followed April 7 Reuters reporting on Russian satellite and cyber support; expired May 16
Correct_Evidentiary_Classification: Post-disclosure continuation of energy-market relief
Russian_Reception_or_Benefit: Preserved Russian transaction value after detailed targeting-support reporting
What_It_Does_Not_Prove: Does not prove the license was connected to the intelligence allegation
Records_Needed: Decision memo; intelligence briefing chronology; estimated Russian revenue; alternative supply options

Title_or_Action: Final identified extension of Russian-origin oil cargo authorization
Primary_Beneficiaries: Energy purchasers, logistics providers and Russian sellers
What_It_Authorized: Continued qualifying delivery and sale authority through the defined period
Predecessor_or_Context: Followed U.S. sanctions against China-based imagery providers; expired June 17
Correct_Evidentiary_Classification: Continued market-stabilization authorization and comparative-consequence evidence
Russian_Reception_or_Benefit: Maintained qualifying Russian oil pathways while China-based targeting providers faced public sanctions
What_It_Does_Not_Prove: Does not establish that Russia was exempt from every consequence or that China and Russia evidence was identical
Records_Needed: Comparative State/Treasury options; transaction volume; Russian fiscal benefit; expiration and enforcement records
